properties.title: Lakeview Heights — 3 BHK Apartments in Whitefield
properties.description:
Lakeview Heights is a ready-to-move gated development off Whitefield Main Road, built around a central landscaped court and a clubhouse. The apartments are laid out so that the living room and the primary bedroom face the open side of the block, which keeps the interiors bright through the day and reduces the need for artificial lighting.

Each tower has two lifts, full power backup for common areas and covered parking at basement level. The clubhouse holds a gymnasium, a swimming pool, a multi-purpose hall and a small library; the podium level carries a jogging track, a badminton court and a children’s play area away from the driveway.

The development sits within a short drive of the technology parks along Whitefield Main Road and Varthur Road, with international schools, multi-speciality hospitals and two shopping centres in the immediate catchment. Purple Line metro stations on Whitefield Main Road have made the commute towards the city centre considerably more predictable than it was.

Two and three-bedroom configurations are available, from 1,180 to 1,860 square feet of super built-up area. This listing is a placeholder record created for the starter seed; the project, its pricing and its approvals are fictional.

properties.title: Nandi Ridge Terraces — 2 and 3 BHK on Sarjapur Road
properties.description:
Nandi Ridge Terraces is an under-construction development set slightly off Sarjapur Road, planned as four towers around a central amenity deck. The first two towers have topped out and are in the finishing stage; the remaining towers follow on a staggered schedule, with possession for the whole development scheduled for mid-2028.

Apartment layouts are two and three-bedroom, sized between 1,090 and 1,720 square feet of super built-up area. Every unit has a utility balcony separated from the living balcony, and the three-bedroom layouts place the primary bedroom on the quieter side of the block, away from the internal driveway.

The amenity deck sits above the parking levels and carries the clubhouse, a swimming pool, a gymnasium, a jogging track and a children’s play area. Rainwater harvesting and a sewage treatment plant are part of the base design, and the common-area lighting runs on a solar-assisted supply.

The corridor puts the technology clusters at Bellandur, Marathahalli and Electronic City within a practical commute. This listing is a placeholder record created for the starter seed; the project, its schedule and its approvals are fictional.

properties.title: Cauvery Green Villas — 4 BHK Villas in Yelahanka
properties.description:
Cauvery Green Villas is a low-density gated layout of four-bedroom villas in Yelahanka, north Bengaluru. Each villa sits on a 2,400 square foot plot with a private garden on two sides, a covered porch for two cars and a service yard set behind the kitchen.

The ground floor holds the living and dining rooms, the kitchen with its utility, a guest bedroom with an attached bathroom and a powder room. Three bedrooms occupy the first floor, each with an attached bathroom, along with a family lounge that opens onto a terrace.

The layout shares a clubhouse with a gymnasium, a multi-purpose hall and a small pool, plus a landscaped park and a jogging loop along the perimeter. Roads within the layout are wide enough for two-way traffic with kerbside visitor parking, and the whole layout runs on an underground service duct.

Yelahanka puts the airport within a comfortable drive while keeping the density and the noise of the technology corridors at a distance. This listing is a placeholder record created for the starter seed; the project and its approvals are fictional.

properties.description:
This fully furnished two-bedroom apartment is on the third floor of a lift-served block in Koramangala, one of the few genuinely walkable neighbourhoods in Bengaluru. The apartment is available immediately and is let unfurnished of personal effects but complete with white goods, wardrobes and the main furniture.

The living room opens onto a balcony overlooking the internal court rather than the road, which keeps it quiet through the evening. The kitchen is modular, with a chimney, a hob and a water purifier already installed, and the utility balcony behind it takes a washing machine.

Both bedrooms have fitted wardrobes and attached bathrooms with geysers. One covered parking bay is allotted, and the block has full power backup for the lift and the common areas, with a limited-load backup for each apartment.

Koramangala’s restaurants, studios and small offices are within walking distance, and the Outer Ring Road is a short drive away. This listing is a placeholder record created for the starter seed; the building and its terms are fictional.

properties.title: Hebbal Skyline — Office Floor for Lease near the Outer Ring Road
properties.description:
This is a warm-shell office floor of 4,200 square feet of carpet area on the ninth level of a grade-A building at Hebbal, where the Outer Ring Road meets the airport corridor. The floor is handed over with a false ceiling, basic lighting, fire detection and a raised access floor; partitions, workstations and the server room are fitted out by the occupier.

The building runs four passenger lifts and a service lift, with a full-load generator backup and a central air-conditioning plant on a variable refrigerant system. Two levels of basement parking serve the tower, with bays allotted per floor and additional visitor parking at grade.

The floor plate is efficient, with the core on one side and a clear span across the rest, so a conventional open plan with meeting rooms along the façade fits without wasted circulation. Both the glazed faces look outward rather than into an adjacent building.

Hebbal is roughly 30 kilometres from the airport and ten from the central business district, which is why the corridor has attracted back-office and engineering teams that need both. This listing is a placeholder record created for the starter seed; the building and its terms are fictional.

localities.name: Whitefield
localities.description:
Whitefield grew from a settlement on the eastern edge of Bengaluru into the city’s best known technology corridor. Technology parks along Whitefield Main Road and Varthur Road employ a large share of east Bengaluru’s workforce, and the residential supply around them ranges from compact two-bedroom apartments to gated villa communities.

The Purple Line metro extension has reduced travel times towards the city centre, and the neighbourhood is well supplied with international schools, multi-speciality hospitals and shopping centres. Buyers looking at Whitefield usually weigh the commute against a wider choice of ready-to-move inventory than most other corridors offer.

localities.name: Sarjapur Road
localities.description:
Sarjapur Road connects the Outer Ring Road at Agara to Sarjapur town, and the stretch in between has absorbed a large share of Bengaluru’s new residential launches. Proximity to the office clusters at Bellandur, Marathahalli and Electronic City makes it a practical choice for dual-income households working in different parts of the city.

The corridor is known for its schools and for gated developments set slightly off the main road. Road widening and the planned metro line are the two factors buyers watch most closely, because both affect the daily commute more than any other variable in this micro-market.

localities.name: Electronic City
localities.description:
Electronic City was Bengaluru’s first planned technology township and still houses some of the largest technology campuses in the country. The elevated expressway from Silk Board keeps the corridor usable at peak hours, and the Yellow Line metro extension is expected to change commuting patterns further.

Housing here is comparatively affordable: compact apartments dominate Phase 1 and Phase 2, with plotted developments further south towards Anekal. The rental market is driven almost entirely by the technology workforce, which makes occupancy steady but also ties demand closely to hiring cycles.

localities.description:
Hebbal sits at the junction of the Outer Ring Road and Bellary Road, which makes it the natural gateway between the city centre and the airport corridor. The lake and the surrounding parkland give the neighbourhood an address value that few north Bengaluru locations match.

Commercial development along the Outer Ring Road has added a working population to what was largely a residential catchment, and premium apartment projects have followed. Buyers here are usually choosing between proximity to the airport and proximity to the central business district, a trade-off Hebbal handles better than most.

localities.name: Koramangala
localities.description:
Koramangala is one of the few genuinely walkable neighbourhoods in Bengaluru. Its numbered blocks mix independent houses, older apartment buildings and a dense layer of restaurants, studios and small offices, which is what keeps demand high whatever the market is doing elsewhere.

New supply is limited, so most transactions are resale or redevelopment. Rental yields are among the strongest in the city, and buyers are typically paying for location and convenience rather than for amenities, which the older stock rarely offers at scale.

localities.name: Yelahanka
localities.description:
Yelahanka was laid out as a satellite town long before the airport moved north, which is why its layouts are wider and greener than most of the city. The airport corridor turned it into one of Bengaluru’s more active residential markets, with villa projects and plotted developments alongside the older layouts.

Lakes, the air force station and a comparatively low building density define the character of the area. Buyers come here for space and for the airport commute; the trade-off is a longer drive to the technology corridors in the east and south.

articles.title: Karnataka RERA: A Practical Guide for Homebuyers
articles.excerpt: What the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act means in Karnataka, what a registration number tells you, and how to read a project page on the regulator’s portal.
articles.content:
Why the Act exists

The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act was written to fix a specific imbalance: a buyer committing a large share of their savings to something that did not yet exist, on the strength of a brochure. It requires most projects to be registered with a state regulator before they are marketed, and it puts the promised specification, the promised area and the promised date on the public record.

What registration actually means

A registration number means the project has been entered with the regulator and that the declarations, approvals and schedule filed with it are available to read. It is not a quality certificate, and it is not an approval of the design. What it gives a buyer is a documented promise that can be compared against what is eventually delivered.

Reading the project page

The regulator’s portal publishes the documents the promoter filed. The ones worth opening are the approved plan, the commencement certificate, the schedule of development and the quarterly progress updates. Compare the number of towers, the number of units and the completion date on the portal against the brochure in front of you. If the two disagree, ask why before anything is signed.

Carpet area, not super built-up area

The Act defines carpet area and requires it to be stated. Super built-up area remains the number most brochures lead with, so the ratio between the two is what tells you how much usable space you are buying. Two apartments advertised at the same super built-up area can differ by a couple of hundred square feet of carpet area.

The escrow requirement

A defined share of the money collected for a project has to sit in a separate account and be drawn only against construction progress, certified by the project’s own professionals. This is the provision aimed squarely at the practice of funding one project out of another’s collections.

Agents are registered too

Anyone facilitating a sale in a registered project is expected to hold a registration of their own. Asking for it is reasonable, and it is a quick way to establish who you are actually dealing with.

If something goes wrong

Complaints go to the regulator or its appellate tribunal rather than to a civil court in the first instance, which is what makes the process usable. Delays, deviations from the sanctioned plan and defects reported within the defect-liability window are the three categories that come up most often.

A short checklist

Verify the registration number on the regulator’s own portal rather than on a brochure. Read the approved plan and the commencement certificate. Compare the carpet area against the super built-up area. Check the declared completion date and the quarterly progress filings. Keep every receipt and every allotment letter. Ask for the agent’s registration.

This article is general guidance written for the starter seed and is not legal advice. Rules, rates and timelines change; confirm the current position with a qualified professional before you act on any of it.

featuredImage.alt: Karnataka RERA: A Practical Guide for Homebuyers

faqs.question: Does every project have to be registered?
faqs.answer: Registration applies to most projects above the thresholds the Act sets for land area and number of units. Smaller developments and projects that were already complete when the Act came into force can fall outside it, which is worth checking rather than assuming.

faqs.question: Is a registration number a guarantee of quality?
faqs.answer: No. It means the project and its declarations are on the public record, which gives you something to compare the delivered product against. It is not an assessment of construction quality.

articles.title: Whitefield Locality Guide for Property Buyers
articles.excerpt: How Whitefield is laid out, what the metro extension changed, which pockets suit which budget, and the questions worth asking before you buy there.
articles.content:
How the neighbourhood is laid out

Whitefield is not one place. The stretch along Whitefield Main Road, the pockets around Varthur and Gunjur, the older layouts near the railway station and the newer developments towards Hoskote all behave like separate micro-markets, with prices, densities and commutes that differ considerably.

What the metro changed

The Purple Line extension turned a commute that was entirely dependent on road conditions into one with a predictable alternative. The effect on prices has been strongest within walking distance of the stations, and it has been most visible in rental demand, where a predictable commute is worth more than an extra amenity.

Ready to move against under construction

Whitefield has an unusually deep stock of completed projects, which means a buyer can compare a finished apartment against a plan rather than only against other plans. Under-construction inventory is usually cheaper per square foot, and the trade-off is the waiting period and the risk attached to it.

Matching the pocket to the budget

Compact two-bedroom apartments in the older layouts sit at the lower end. Gated developments with full amenity decks along the main road sit in the middle. Villa layouts towards Varthur and Gunjur sit at the top. Within each band, the distance to the nearest arterial road explains most of the price difference.

Schools, hospitals and daily life

The catchment holds several international schools and multi-speciality hospitals, plus two large shopping centres. For families this is often the deciding factor: the daily radius is short enough that a household does not need to cross the city for anything routine.

What to check before buying

Water is the first question — whether the project runs on corporation supply, on borewells or on tankers, and what that costs each month. Check the approach road and whether it floods. Walk the route to the nearest metro station rather than trusting a map. Ask the association, not the sales office, about maintenance charges and the sinking fund.

Rental market

Demand is driven by the technology workforce, which makes occupancy steady but ties it to hiring cycles. Furnished two and three-bedroom apartments near the stations let fastest. Yields are moderate rather than spectacular; the argument for Whitefield has historically been liquidity rather than yield.

The short version

Whitefield suits buyers who want completed stock, a short daily radius and a resale market with real depth. It suits less well a buyer who wants low density or a short drive to the central business district. Pick the pocket before the project, and walk the commute before signing anything.

This article is general guidance written for the starter seed. Prices, projects and infrastructure timelines change; confirm the current position before you act on any of it.

featuredImage.alt: Whitefield Locality Guide for Property Buyers

faqs.question: Is Whitefield better for buying or for renting out?
faqs.answer: Both markets are active. Owner-occupiers value the depth of completed stock and the short daily radius; investors value the steady rental demand from the technology workforce, though yields are moderate rather than exceptional.

faqs.question: How much does the metro station distance matter?
faqs.answer: More than most amenities. A walkable distance to a station shows up in both rent and resale, because it replaces an unpredictable road commute with a predictable one.

articles.title: Home Loan Eligibility and EMI Planning Basics
articles.excerpt: How lenders decide what you can borrow, what the loan-to-value ratio leaves you to fund, and how tenure and rate move the monthly instalment.
articles.content:
Two numbers decide the loan

Every home loan decision comes down to two limits, and the lower of the two is what you get. The first is what your income supports; the second is what the property supports. Understanding both before you shortlist saves a great deal of disappointment later.

What your income supports

Lenders work from a ratio between your total monthly obligations and your monthly income. Existing instalments — a car loan, a personal loan, the minimum on a credit card — are counted against you, so clearing a small loan before applying can raise the sanction more than a salary increment would. A co-applicant’s income is usually added, which is why joint applications are common.

What the property supports

The loan-to-value ratio caps the loan against the property’s assessed value, and the assessed value is not always the agreed price. The gap, together with stamp duty, registration and any charges the builder collects separately, is what you have to fund yourself. Budgeting only for the down payment is the most common planning mistake.

How the instalment moves

The monthly instalment responds to three things: the amount, the rate and the tenure. Lengthening the tenure lowers the instalment and raises the total interest paid, sometimes dramatically. Shortening it does the reverse. A small difference in rate matters more over twenty years than it appears to over one.

Fixed against floating

A floating rate moves with the lender’s benchmark; a fixed rate does not, usually in exchange for starting higher. Most borrowers take floating rates and manage the risk by keeping some capacity to prepay. What matters more than the choice is knowing how the benchmark resets and how often.

Prepayment

Prepaying early in the schedule removes far more interest than prepaying late, because the early instalments are mostly interest. Ask, before signing, whether prepayment carries a charge and whether the lender reduces the tenure or the instalment by default — the first saves much more.

The documents

Expect to provide identity and address proof, income proof, bank statements and the property papers. Self-employed applicants are assessed on returns and on the business’s banking, which takes longer. Keeping a clean set ready shortens the process more than any negotiation does.

A sensible sequence

Check your credit record first. Work out the total cash you need, not just the down payment. Get an in-principle sanction before you commit to a property. Compare the effective rate and the fees together rather than the headline rate alone. Then decide the tenure by what you can service comfortably, not by what the calculator allows.

This article is general guidance written for the starter seed and is not financial advice. Rates, ratios and charges vary by lender and change over time; confirm the current position with the lender before you act on any of it.

featuredImage.alt: Home Loan Eligibility and EMI Planning Basics

faqs.question: Does a co-applicant always increase the sanction?
faqs.answer: Usually, because the incomes are added — but the co-applicant’s existing obligations are added too. If they carry significant instalments of their own, the net effect can be smaller than expected.

faqs.question: Is a longer tenure always cheaper?
faqs.answer: Only month to month. The instalment falls, but the total interest paid over the life of the loan rises, often substantially. Choose the shortest tenure whose instalment you can service comfortably.

faqs.question: How do I start a property search with Squares N Acres?
faqs.answer: Tell us the locality, the budget and the configuration you have in mind through any enquiry form on the site. An advisor will come back with a shortlist drawn from our curated inventory and arrange site visits.

faqs.question: Do you charge buyers a fee?
faqs.answer: Our commercial terms are agreed before any engagement begins and are explained in writing. Ask the advisor handling your enquiry for the current terms.

faqs.question: Can you help me sell or let out my property?
faqs.answer: Yes. Send us the details through the enquiry form and an advisor will discuss valuation, documentation and how the listing would be marketed.

faqs.question: What documents does a tenant usually need?
faqs.answer: Identity proof, address proof and employment or income proof are the usual set, along with the agreed deposit. Individual owners may ask for more.

faqs.question: Can you help arrange a home loan?
faqs.answer: We can introduce you to lenders and help you compare indicative terms. The sanction, the rate and the final terms are decided by the lender.

faqs.question: What should I check in the title documents?
faqs.answer: The chain of title, the current owner’s right to sell, any encumbrance on the property and the approvals for the building. A qualified advocate should review the set before you commit.

faqs.question: How do I verify a project’s RERA registration?
faqs.answer: Look the registration number up on the state regulator’s own portal rather than relying on a brochure, and read the approvals and progress filings published there.

faqs.question: Can a non-resident Indian buy property in Bengaluru?
faqs.answer: Non-resident Indians may buy residential and commercial property subject to the rules in force, with specific restrictions on agricultural land. Confirm the current position with a qualified professional before committing.
